definitions.gloss: forcing someone to do something; coercion; compulsion
definitions.explanation: The act of pressuring or compelling someone to do something against their will.

examples.japanese: {無理強|むりじ}いはしないで⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧。
⟦お{酒|さけ}→お酒：01045_osake⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{無理強|むりじ}い⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦よくない→いい：00118_ii⟧。
examples.english: Forcing someone to drink is not good.

examples.japanese: ⟦{子|こ}→子：09851_ko⟧ども⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{勉強|べんきょう}→勉強：00770_benkyou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{無理強|むりじ}い⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{逆効果|ぎゃくこうか}→逆効果：14315_gyakukouka⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: Forcing a child to study can sometimes have the opposite effect.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{無理|むり}→無理：01558_muri⟧ (unreasonable, impossible) + {強|し}い (forcing). Describes the act of pressuring someone into doing something they don't want to do.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {無理強|むりじ}い⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to force; to coerce
- {無理強|むりじ}いはしない: to not force (someone)
- ⟦お{酒|さけ}→お酒：01045_osake⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{無理強|むりじ}い: forcing someone to drink alcohol
- {無理強|むりじ}い⟦される→する：00392_suru⟧: to be forced/coerced

USAGE:
Often appears in contexts about social pressure, such as drinking culture, eating, or work demands. The ⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ form ({無理強|むりじ}い⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧) is commonly used as a verb meaning 'to force.' The word carries a clearly negative connotation—it always implies that the pressure is unwelcome.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{強制|きょうせい}→強制：12500_kyousei⟧: compulsion — more formal and official; used for legal or institutional contexts
- ⟦{強要|きょうよう}→強要：12538_kyouyou⟧: coercion, demand — stronger and more aggressive than {無理強|むりじ}い
- ⟦{押|お}し{付|つ}ける→押し付ける：04236_oshitsukeru⟧: to force upon — more casual; focuses on imposing things (opinions, tasks) on others
